title: ～たところ — “have just ～ed”
summary: Attached to the ta-form of a verb, it shows the action has just ended. Often used with 今 or ちょうど.

patterns.gloss: Verb ta-form + ところだ (食べたところだ)

body.p: It points to the moment just after the action ended and before the next begins. ご飯を食べたところです means “I have just finished eating.”
V dictionary form + ところ is “about to do”, and V-ている + ところ is “in the middle of”. Learn the three together to tell them apart.

examples.ja: 今（いま）、ご飯（はん）を食（た）べたところです。
examples.romaji: Ima, gohan o tabeta tokoro desu.
examples.tr: I have just finished eating now.

examples.ja: ちょうど家（いえ）を出（で）たところです。
examples.romaji: Chōdo ie o deta tokoro desu.

examples.ja: 今（いま）、宿題（しゅくだい）が終（お）わったところだ。
examples.romaji: Ima, shukudai ga owatta tokoro da.
examples.tr: I've just finished my homework now.

pitfalls: It covers a shorter time than たばかり (not for days ago).
Attach it to the ta-form, not the ます-form.
